title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GORDY'S BOWLS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gordy Pike, a butcher from Concord, New Hampshire.
This winter, he had to make one hundred soup bowls out of mud.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: NOT MY THING
segments.quote: It is never too late to give up our prejudices.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: Every February, the fire station holds a soup supper. Pay what you can, keep the bowl.
This year, Gordy's wife Linda signed him up for pottery class to make the bowls.
Pottery? said Gordy. That's for fancy people in scarves.
Linda opened his dad's old copy of Walden, by Henry David Thoreau:
It is never too late to give up our prejudices.
So Gordy put on an apron with no pork on it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: FLYING CLAY
segments.quote: The creation of something new is not accomplished by the intellect but by the play instinct acting from inner necessity.
segments.author: Carl Jung
lines: The teacher, seventy-seven-year-old Miss Bea, dropped clay on a spinning wheel.
Gordy read the manual twice, and the clay flew off and hit the ceiling.
Miss Bea laughed and quoted the Swiss doctor Carl Jung:
The creation of something new is not accomplished by the intellect but by the play instinct acting from inner necessity.
So Gordy stopped thinking and played. His first bowl looked like a sad hat. He loved it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: SORE HANDS
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: By December, his hands ached, and forty bowls had flopped like pancakes.
Linda taped a line from Benjamin Franklin to the fridge:
Constant dropping wears away stones.
So he made just two bowls a night. Every night. Like water on a rock.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE RUSH
segments.quote: It is quality, rather than quantity, that matters.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: In January he was fifty bowls short, so he cranked them out like hamburger patties.
Miss Bea held one up. Thin as paper. She read from Seneca, the Roman thinker:
It is quality, rather than quantity, that matters.
Gordy slowed down. Every bowl could hold hot soup.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: SOUP NIGHT
segments.quote: The best sauce in the world is hunger.
segments.author: Miguel de Cervantes
lines: Supper night came. Ninety-four bowls, some crooked. He was sure people would laugh.
Then a snowplow driver grabbed the most crooked one and asked for seconds.
An old firefighter grinned and quoted Cervantes, who wrote Don Quixote:
The best sauce in the world is hunger.
Nobody cared about the bowls. Gordy ladled soup until midnight.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: NEXT YEAR
segments.quote: He that plants trees, loves others besides himself.
segments.author: Thomas Fuller
lines: Afterward, Danny from his meat counter asked how you make a bowl.
Gordy remembered a saying collected by Thomas Fuller, an English doctor:
He that plants trees, loves others besides himself.
So Gordy bought a used wheel, and now he teaches every Saturday.
Next February, the fire station had two hundred bowls.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Drop the old opinion. Play. Keep at it. Slow down. Feed people. Teach someone.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Drop the old opinion. Play. Keep at it. Slow down. Feed people. Teach someone.
I made a coffee mug once. It holds exactly one sip.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
